title: Grade 6 Math — Wed, Jun 25
description: Mensuration — Day 3 of 5: Area of parallelogram, rhombus and composite figures
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Area of a parallelogram: base=14 cm, height=8 cm
questions.explanation: Area of parallelogram = base × height = 14 × 8 = 112 cm². Note: height is the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides, NOT the slant side.

questions.question: Area of a rhombus with diagonals d₁=10 cm and d₂=8 cm
questions.explanation: Area of rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 cm².

questions.question: A parallelogram has area 120 cm² and base 15 cm. Height =
questions.explanation: Area = base × height → 120 = 15 × h → h = 8 cm.

A composite figure = a rectangle (12×8 cm) + a triangle on top (base=12, height=5 cm). Total area =
questions.explanation: Rectangle = 12×8 = 96 cm². Triangle = ½×12×5 = 30 cm². Total = 96 + 30 = 126 cm².

questions.question: A floor made of rhombus-shaped tiles (d₁=20 cm, d₂=16 cm). How many tiles cover 32,000 cm²?
questions.explanation: Tile area = ½ × 20 × 16 = 160 cm². Number = 32,000 ÷ 160 = 200 tiles.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are in ratio 3:4. Shorter diagonal = 9 cm. Area =
questions.explanation: Diagonals 3:4 → shorter = 9 → longer = 12. Area = ½ × 9 × 12 = 54 cm².

questions.question: A figure consists of a square (side 10 cm) and a triangle (base 10 cm, height 8 cm). Area =
questions.explanation: Square = 10² = 100 cm². Triangle = ½×10×8 = 40 cm². Total = 140 cm².

questions.question: A parallelogram has the same area as a rectangle (18 cm × 12 cm). If its height is 9 cm, base =
questions.explanation: Rectangle area = 18×12 = 216 cm². Parallelogram: b×h = 216 → b×9 = 216 → b = 24 cm.

questions.question: A shaded region: large rectangle (20×15 cm) with a parallelogram (base=10, height=8 cm) cut out. Shaded area =
questions.explanation: Large rectangle = 20×15 = 300 cm². Parallelogram = 10×8 = 80 cm². Shaded = 300 − 80 = 220 cm².

questions.question: A kite (which is a special quadrilateral) has diagonals 15 cm and 10 cm. Area =
questions.explanation: A kite's area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ (same formula as rhombus) = ½ × 15 × 10 = 75 cm².

A parallelogram has base 25 cm and height 12 cm. A triangle is cut from it (base 25 cm, height 8 cm). Remaining area =
questions.explanation: Parallelogram = 25×12 = 300 cm². Triangle = ½×25×8 = 100 cm². Remaining = 300 − 100 = 200 cm².

questions.question: Why is the area of a parallelogram = base × height (not base × slant side)?
options: Both formulas give the same result
The HEIGHT is the perpendicular distance between the bases — it represents the actual vertical extent; the slant side would overcount area if the shape leans
The slant side is always longer
Area formula only applies to rectangles
questions.explanation: A parallelogram can be rearranged into a rectangle: cut a triangle from one end and move it to the other. The resulting rectangle = base × perpendicular height. The slant side is longer than the height and gives a wrong (larger) area.

questions.question: A figure is made of two triangles sharing a base (like a kite): triangle 1 (base=12, h=5), triangle 2 (base=12, h=7). Total area =
questions.explanation: Triangle 1 = ½×12×5 = 30 cm². Triangle 2 = ½×12×7 = 42 cm². Total = 72 cm².
